clue.text: Enumeration of facts amended in article

indicators.note: something amended has been altered, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of facts gets corrected within a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link; 'amended' rearranges ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a detailed spoken or written account listing things one by one.

clue.text: Enrolled in navy, Eastern servicemen roll over and quit

indicators.note: pieces enrolled in the navy are placed inside its abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: rolling over turns the servicemen's letters back to front

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Recruits from the East join the navy, then turn tail and leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll over' turns only the servicemen; 'Enrolled in' then puts the Eastern letter and those turned letters inside the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a post, which is to quit it.

clue.text: Part of testimonial

definitions.meaning: a role played by an actor
a written reference vouching for someone's nature

explanation.definitionFit: A character is a role in a play and also an old word for a reference from an employer.

clue.text: Walked out, for no good and acceptable reason, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word in the run before it

explanation.surface: Someone stormed off without a good or acceptable excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walked out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' is the start of the run whose last letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Trodden is the past participle of tread, meaning walked upon.

clue.text: Throw up a Liverpudlian stew

parts.note: to lob is to throw something high in the air
Scouse is the nickname for a person from Liverpool

explanation.surface: A Liverpool stew so bad it makes someone vomit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' looks like being sick but means throw high. Scouse, the Liverpool nickname, comes from the name of this sailors' stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobscouse is a meat and vegetable stew traditionally eaten by sailors and in Liverpool.

clue.text: Indicate checking of carpet

definitions.meaning: mark an item as checked on a list
as a verb, to reprimand someone

explanation.definitionFit: To tick off is both to mark items as done with a tick and, colloquially, to scold someone.

clue.text: Poisonous substance in corned beef?

parts.note: corned beef is an ox in a tin, so the letters of the beast sit inside those of the can

explanation.surface: A warning about something nasty lurking in tinned meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Corned beef comes as ox in tin, so T(OX)IN spells the word for a poison.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxin is a poison produced by a living organism.

clue.text: Earthenware saucer — am I careless holding it?

indicators.note: the words are holding the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Someone worries they have been clumsy carrying a pottery saucer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramic describes pottery made from fired clay, such as earthenware.

clue.text: Nestling down in the middle with permit

indicators.note: in the middle points to the central letters of the word down

parts.note: to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A young bird settled in soft feathers, with permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' suggests a bird's soft feathers but only gives its middle letters OW.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, a nestling still in the nest.

clue.text: Patty, a rather strange person seen on set

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece seen on another sits above it

parts.note: a queer fish or odd fish is an eccentric person
to cake is to set hard

explanation.surface: An odd person spotted on a film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' suggests a film set but means harden, as mud cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishcake is a flat round patty of fish and potato.

clue.text: Act unconvincingly in dog fight

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, to shadow them
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Someone is hamming it up during a dog fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is a verb meaning follow, not an animal; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow-box is to spar with no opponent, making a show of fighting without real conviction.

clue.text: Governs game in Australia

explanation.definitionFit: Rules means governs as a verb, and Aussie Rules is Australia's own football code.

clue.text: Good money for a piano

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A good sum of cash paid for a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good money' reads as a decent price but splits into G and RAND; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is a large concert piano with horizontal strings.

clue.text: Nice mac — it looks different on the screen

indicators.note: the letters of the words before take on a different look, being rearranged

explanation.surface: A nice raincoat looks unlike itself when filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinematic means relating to films, which are shown on the screen.

clue.text: With ironic intent and a mouthful of meat

definitions.meaning: taken literally, an ox's tongue placed in cheek, both cuts of meat

explanation.definitionFit: Tongue-in-cheek describes something said with ironic rather than sincere intent.

clue.text: Lawyers may be so employed, whatever happens

explanation.definitionFit: In any case means whatever happens, and literally describes lawyers engaged on any legal case.

clue.text: Happy-go-lucky midshipman available

parts.note: Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Frederick Marryat's novel
going means available, as in a job going

explanation.surface: A carefree young naval officer is free.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Midshipman Easy is an 1836 sea novel by Captain Marryat.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-going describes a relaxed, carefree, happy-go-lucky temperament.

clue.text: Chain apt to break under pressure

indicators.note: a chain apt to break comes apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chain that is likely to snap when strained.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pinch means if necessary, when pushed or under pressure.

clue.text: Article inserted in gramophone parts to effect complete reversal

indicators.note: inserted in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: turntables are the rotating plates of record players
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Fitting something into a record player to reverse it completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn the tables is to reverse a situation so the loser becomes the winner.

clue.text: Emblem in the list, after revision

indicators.note: after revision the words are rewritten in a new order

explanation.surface: A badge appears in a list once it has been revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is the national emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: Crane fly has more than one position in the field

definitions.text: Crane fly has more than one
definitions.meaning: the daddy-... has many ..., so one of them is singular
a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side

explanation.walkthrough: LONG LEG is a cricket fielding position; crane flies are known as daddy-long-legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Long leg is a deep fielding position in cricket, and a crane fly's limbs are each a long leg.

clue.text: Watch a number of races finish

parts.note: the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the series of motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Someone watches several races come to their conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man TT is a set of motorcycle races held each year.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to watch over or be present to see something.

clue.text: Maiden is engaged in minor form of clairvoyance

indicators.note: pieces engaged in another are held inside it

parts.note: paltry means minor or trivial
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl takes up a lesser type of fortune-telling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' suggests a young woman but is the cricket M; 'minor form' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmistry is fortune-telling by reading the lines of the hand, a kind of clairvoyance.

clue.text: Joins course

definitions.meaning: a golf course by the sea

explanation.definitionFit: Links means joins as a verb, and a links is a seaside golf course.

clue.text: Cross river, heading for Yorkshire

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone crosses a river on the way to Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning irritable. The Test is a Hampshire trout river.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy means irritable or short-tempered, which is cross.

clue.text: Black chessman — but not the king

indicators.note: but not removes the piece that follows from the one before

parts.note: the knight is a chess piece
K is the chess notation for the king

explanation.surface: A dark chess piece that is not the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' looks like the colour of the chess piece but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is darkness, so as a noun it serves for black.

clue.text: Players I entered in books

indicators.note: entered in places one piece within another

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a collection of books
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A performer's name is written into the record books.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians, a band of players.

clue.text: Minor shopping centre covered by expresses on the way back

indicators.note: a piece covered by another sits inside it
on the way back reads the word's letters in reverse

parts.note: emits means gives out or expresses
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A small shopping centre served by express trains heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns only 'expresses'; 'covered by' then places the shopping centre just after the first letter of that turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-time means minor or unimportant.

clue.text: Yorkshire upset when two kings abandoned footwear

indicators.note: upset scrambles the letters of the county name

parts.note: K and R both stand for king, K in chess and R for Rex

explanation.surface: Yorkshire is upset when two monarchs leave their shoes behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes K and R from YORKSHIRE; 'upset' rearranges the remaining YOSHIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosiery means stockings and socks, worn on the feet and legs.

clue.text: In conclusion, challenge is taken on

indicators.note: In places one piece within another

parts.note: the end is the conclusion
a gage is a pledge thrown down as a challenge

explanation.surface: At the end a challenge is accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In conclusion' looks like a phrase meaning finally but splits into the insertion and END.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaged means taken on, as a worker hired.
